options: consecutive_wrong ≥ 2 on one concept within a session, and dwell ≥ 3× the LEARNER'S OWN median without an attempt
any wrong answer, and any page refresh
two different concepts wrong in one week, and dwell ≥ 3× the cohort median
items.explanation: Wrong answers must chain on the SAME concept (one wrong is noise); the dwell baseline is personal, not cohort-global — penalising careful readers is the classic false positive. (obj-19-a)

items.prompt: A telemetry POST arrives with consent: absent. What does the system do?
options: HTTP 403, nothing stored, a consent_missing receipt — the wall fails CLOSED: absent means no, and the refusal is an artifact
Stores it pseudonymised and asks for consent later
items.explanation: Consent precedes storage, fail-closed: missing/malformed/stale all refuse, and the refusal receipt proves the wall held — auditable ethics. (obj-19-b)

items.prompt: Which of these is NEVER stored under the course's telemetry schema?
options: dwell samples and the consent version
items.explanation: No names anywhere — handles are hashed at capture; the demo, digests and receipts carry hashes only. The ethics lives in the schema, not a policy PDF. (obj-19-b)

items.prompt: A stuck signal fires for a learner who consented Tuesday and withdrew Thursday. What does Friday's system do?
options: Sends help anyway — consent was given once
Stores nothing new and sends nothing; the withdrawal ends the permission. The refusal is receipted and the learner keeps full course access
Sends one final micro-lesson as a courtesy
items.explanation: The wall respects time, not just presence — and opting out never costs access: leaving changes nothing about the course. (obj-19-b)
